A.explanation: Uses $pV_0$ instead of work done. Only the increase $V_F - V_0$ contributes to expansion work, not the starting volume $V_0$.

B.explanation: Has no pressure $p$ and has units of $1/\text{pressure}$, so it cannot be $\text{work}/\text{energy}$ and cannot be efficiency.

C.explanation: Work at constant pressure is $p(V_F - V_0)$, so efficiency $= p(V_F - V_0)/q$, which is useful output energy divided by input energy.

D.explanation: Uses volume change correctly but omits pressure $p$, so numerator is a volume not an energy and the ratio is not dimensionless.

hints: Notice what is input and what is useful output: thermal energy $q$ is supplied, and the useful effect is expansion from $V_0$ to $V_F$ at pressure $p$.
Recall efficiency $=$ useful output energy divided by total input energy, and for a gas at constant pressure work $= p \times$ change in volume.
Form the change in volume $V_F - V_0$, multiply by $p$ to get work in joules, then divide by $q$ and check which option matches.
walkthrough: Identify the energy transfer: input energy is the supplied thermal energy $q$, and useful output energy is the mechanical work done by the gas on the piston.
State the efficiency rule: $\text{efficiency} = \text{useful output energy} / \text{total input energy} = W/q$.
State the work rule for constant pressure: $W = p\Delta V = p(V_F - V_0)$, because the piston moves through the volume increase $V_F - V_0$ against pressure $p$.
Substitute into efficiency: $\text{efficiency} = p(V_F - V_0)/q$. The $p \times$ volume term has units of energy, so the ratio is dimensionless as required. This is option C.
